# Phase 4 results: promotion allocation under budget (generated by scripts/40_phase4_allocation.py)

## Assumptions (all parameters in src/allocation.py and the app)

- Margin rate 30% of shelf price; feature slot $150/store-week; display $100/store-week; price cuts cost the mean discount depth of that promo type on every unit sold (baseline + incremental).
- Lift per (product, promo type) = sum incremental / sum baseline over Phase 1 events (>= 30 events, else category-type lift); the risk-averse run uses the 2.5th percentile of the event-level bootstrap.
- 27,159 candidate (store, product, promo type) triples; one promotion at most per store-product per week.

Mean discount depth by type used for costing: display+price=20%, feature+display+price=25%, feature+price=24%, price_only=20%

## Point estimate vs risk-averse allocation at a $20,000 weekly budget

| promo_type   |   point_estimate |   risk_averse (CI lower bound) |
|:-------------|-----------------:|-------------------------------:|
| price_only   |              725 |                            873 |
| display_only |                6 |                              2 |

Expected incremental units by category:

| category              |   point_estimate |   risk_averse |
|:----------------------|-----------------:|--------------:|
| COLD CEREAL           |            12875 |         10065 |
| FROZEN PIZZA          |             4182 |          5436 |
| ORAL HYGIENE PRODUCTS |              201 |           490 |

- 89% of the point-estimate picks survive in the risk-averse solution.
- Point-estimate plan: 731 promotions, expected 17,258 incremental units (lower bound 13,656).
- Risk-averse plan: 875 promotions, expected 15,990 incremental units (lower bound 12,985).
- The risk-averse plan gives up expected volume to buy a higher guaranteed floor: it shifts away from product-type cells whose lift is estimated from few events (wide CI) toward well-measured ones. That is the point of solving it twice.

Share of picks whose lift came from product-level (vs category fallback) estimates:

| level    |   point |   risk_averse |
|:---------|--------:|--------------:|
| product  |    100% |          100% |
| category |      0% |            0% |
